To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the GWA analyses identified significantly associated SNPs on the genome-wide level with the trait NEC under limited Fe regimes and that the trait NEC is a good indicator of Fe-efficiency under limited Fe regimes.
the GWA analyses under both Fe regimes identified significantly associated SNPs for NEC, RW, SPAD, and SP3, which were located in genes and/or in recognition sites of transcription regulators.
we identified 18 significantly associated SNPs on the genome-wide level under limited Fe conditions and 17 significantly associated SNPs under adequate Fe conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of candidate genes for Fe-efficiency, and the identification of SNPs for the development of molecular markers in maize breeding programs.

the identification of SNPs which are significantly associated with morphological or physiological traits under limited or adequate Fe regimes, which might serve as a basis for future functional analyses and marker assisted selection.
the first genome-wide association study on iron homeostasis traits of a maize association population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GWA mapping is a powerful tool for the identification of genes or regulatory elements involved in Fe-efficiency in maize.
the identified genes or SNPs are involved in the Fe homeostasis in maize.

the GWA approach is a powerful tool in order to identify candidate SNPs for the trait NEC, RW, and SDW under limited and adequate conditions, and for the trait H 2O and SPAD value under adequate conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to identify SNPs associated with Fe-efficiency traits on a genome-wide and fine-mapping level.
the combination of fine-mapping with the GWA approach is an efficient tool for identifying genes and candidate genes for Fe efficiency in maize.
the GWA approach is an efficient method to detect SNPs associated with morphological or physiological traits under different Fe regimes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GWA analyses in maize are a powerful tool for the identification of candidate genes involved in the formation of morphological and physiological responses to limited and adequate Fe availability.
the GWA approach is a powerful tool to dissect the genetic basis of Fe-efficiency.
GWA mapping is an effective approach to dissect the correlation between phenotypic traits.
